security_frame.attacker: Privileged software (Caliptra firmware) able to write the HMAC control register and read the HMAC tag register, the ordinary interface any HMAC client uses.
security_frame.precondition: A previous HMAC operation has completed, so digest_valid_reg is set and the tag register holds that operation's result.
security_frame.input: An ordinary HMAC INIT to start a new operation.
security_frame.protected_asset: The HMAC tag of the previous operation, which may be computed over a different key or a different message than the caller of the new operation is entitled to.
security_frame.security_property: Starting a new operation must invalidate the previous result before the new one is available, so that a valid-signalled tag always corresponds to the operation the reader believes it started.
security_frame.modification: In hmac_core.sv, the init_cmd arm of CTRL_IDLE drives digest_valid_new = 1'b0 at line 340 but never asserts digest_valid_we, so the register update at lines 202-203 never happens and digest_valid_reg keeps its stale value of 1.

security_feature_bypassed: Invalidation of the previous HMAC result when a new operation starts, the interlock that makes tag_valid mean the tag belongs to the operation the reader started
proof_goal: Show that the init_cmd arm drives the new value of digest_valid_reg without the write enable its register update requires, that this is the single unpaired site in a file whose every other FSM arm pairs them, and that adding the missing enable makes the same testbench reject the claim.

proof_style.primary: structural audit of the audited RTL against its own idiom
secondary: directed unit-level simulation of hmac_core with cover counters
negative control on a patched scratch copy

minimum_attack_sequence: A previous HMAC operation completes, so digest_valid_reg is 1 and the tag register holds that operation's digest.
Software issues an ordinary INIT to start a new operation.
The init_cmd arm computes digest_valid_new = 0 but omits digest_valid_we, so the register update at lines 202-203 does not fire and digest_valid_reg stays 1.
tag_valid stays asserted and tag keeps presenting the previous operation's H2 digest while the new operation is still running.
A reader that polls for valid and then reads the tag receives the previous operation's result and accepts it as the new one.
expected_evidence: hmac_core.sv:340 drives digest_valid_new = 1'b0 inside the init_cmd arm, and no digest_valid_we assignment appears in that arm (hmac_core.sv:339-343).
hmac_core.sv:202-203 updates digest_valid_reg only when digest_valid_we is asserted, so a new value without the enable is discarded.
The file has exactly 2 assignments to digest_valid_reg: the reset arm at hmac_core.sv:185 and the enabled update at hmac_core.sv:203. There is no other path that could clear it.
In-file control: a computed census pairing every digest_valid_new drive with a digest_valid_we assertion within 3 lines finds 7 drives and 6 pairings, with exactly 1 unpaired site, at line 340.
The next_cmd arm immediately below, at hmac_core.sv:346-347, drives the same variable and does assert the enable, so the correct form is present four lines away.
hmac_core.sv:111-112 makes both tag and tag_valid depend on digest_valid_reg, so a stale 1 exposes the previous digest as valid.
In simulation, with digest_valid_reg set to stand in for a completed prior operation, an INIT leaves it asserted, while a NEXT clears it.
With the missing enable added in a scratch copy, the identical testbench sees digest_valid_reg clear on INIT, the stale-valid cover counter falls to zero, and the self-check fails.
success_criteria: Every structural gate holds, including the computed census whose sole unpaired site is the line under test.
The simulation shows digest_valid_reg surviving an INIT, with the NEXT-clears observation passing in the same run as a control.
The negative control fails on corrected RTL with the stale-valid cover counter at zero, while the NEXT-clears observation still passes.
The finding is anchored on the audited tree's own value/enable pairing convention, not on any external comparison.
